asof: Settles Mon 26 Oct 2026 · written Tue 27 Oct
headline: SR3 adds back 2027 hikes into the FOMC, peaking at 4.655% in U7; consensus still sees one more move. Keep fading 2027.
summary: The strip sold off Monday, led by the 2027 contracts: implied rates rose 4.5–5.5bp in H7–U7, led by SR3M7 (+5.5bp to 4.615%), while U6 (+0.5bp) and Z6 (+2bp) barely moved and the 2029 contracts added only 0.5–1.5bp. That cuts into, but does not undo, October's rally: 2027 contracts remain 16–24bp lower in rate than at the 30 September (modelled) settle, Z7 the most at −23.9bp. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.655%, 73.5bp above the latest 3.92% SOFR fixing, with 17.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. Economists are far less hawkish: all 100 in Reuters' poll see a December hike, and most of the Fed's September projections stop one hike later, at 4.00–4.25%.
drivers: With no data out, desks leaned toward a hawkish hold on Wednesday: Deutsche Bank expects a hawkish message even without a move, and BMO expects at least one dissent from Hammack. The 2-year yield rose 3.2bp to 4.712%, its largest two-day gain (7.6bp) since 24 September, and M7 led the strip at +5.5bp.
A soft start to $213bn of note supply

The $69bn 2-year auction cleared at 4.708% with a 0.3bp tail, a 2.59 bid-to-cover (2.63 last time) and indirects at 45.7% against 57.8%. The $70bn 5-year (Tue), $30bn 2-year FRN (Wed) and $44bn 7-year (Thu) follow, all settling on 2 November.
Oil gave back the spike, not the premium

Brent traded near $110 early on Iran diplomacy but recovered to settle only $0.91 lower at $115.81, with WTI down $1.51 at $101.76, as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply risk in place. That oil could not hold a 6% drop helps explain why the front end did not rally.

SOFR fixed at 3.92% for 23 October, the highest print since the September hike and 4bp over EFFR (3.88%), with the 99th percentile at 4.00%. About 44% of SR3U6's quarter is now fixed; month-end and the 2 November coupon settlements are the next test.
spreads: The curve steepened in the whites on Monday as 2027 sold off more than December: U6/Z6 +26bp (+1.5bp on the day), Z6/H7 +25.5bp (+2.5bp) and H7/M7 +16bp (+1bp), while M7/U7 slipped to +4bp and U7/Z7 to −2bp (−1bp each). Month to date the whites remain much flatter (U6/Z6 −6.3bp, Z6/H7 −6bp, Z6/Z7 −14.1bp to +43.5bp). The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 2bp to +12bp as M7 took the brunt of the selloff, while M7/U7/Z7 held at +6bp. Past the peak, the reds and greens show 1–3bp of easing per quarter: Z7/Z8 −9.5bp and U7/Z8 −11.5bp (both a little more inverted, −1.5bp and −2.5bp on the day), Z8/Z9 −6bp; no month-to-date base exists for the 2028–29 contracts, whose settle history starts 22 October.
fed: Fed funds futures, last recorded at Friday's close, price 2.5bp for Wednesday (about 10% odds of a hike), 21.5bp cumulative by December (a 79% chance of at least one hike), 43.9bp by March, 61.3bp by June and a 68.5bp peak at the September 2027 FOMC (implied EFFR 4.565%). That is down from 26.5bp, 52.1bp and a 74.5bp peak a week earlier and from 30.6bp, 63.4bp and 94bp at the end of September. SR3 is a little more hawkish after Monday: U7 at 4.655% sits about 9bp over the ZQ peak, of which roughly 4bp is the SOFR–EFFR basis and the rest Monday's 4.5bp selloff. Consensus is one hike: 94 of 100 Reuters economists see a hold this week and all 100 a December move, and in September 12 of 18 projections showed one more hike and four showed two. The market still carries roughly 45bp of 2027 tightening that most forecasters do not.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 3.5bp against at +41.5bp after Monday's 2027-led selloff, but still 9.3bp narrower than at end-September and 6.5bp from the stop. Z6 holds the December hike everyone expects, while M7 carries the extra 2027 hikes neither the dots nor the Street project; a hold without guidance and a 3.1% core PCE in line should let M7 recover. No change to levels.
ideas.risk: A hawkish Warsh or dissents that validate a hiking path into 2027 would widen the spread toward the +48bp stop.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open and 1.5bp in favour at −9.5bp: Monday's selloff hit Z7 (+3.5bp) more than Z8 (+2bp), exactly the move this hedge is meant to cover. If the Fed does take SOFR past 4.6% into $115 oil, the easing that follows is likely larger than the 17.5bp now priced from the peak to Z9. Keep at about half the core size.
ideas.risk: A 'higher for longer' plateau through 2028 with no cuts would push the spread back toward flat.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: About 44% of U6's quarter is fixed and the latest fixing printed 3.92%, above the 3.88% EFFR, so funding pressure can only cost a long while only 2.5bp of a hike is priced for Wednesday. U6 moved just 0.5bp on Monday; revisit after the FOMC and the month-end prints.
ideas.risk: A surprise hike on Wednesday would cost U6 roughly 10bp; a dovish surprise would lift it only a few bp.

watch: A second soft auction would extend Monday's 2027 selloff.
Hold expected (2.5bp priced); hawkish dissents would firm December and challenge the core trade.
Core PCE seen at 3.1% y/y and GDP near 3.1–3.2%; a hot core print lifts H7–U7.
ECI seen at 0.8%; month-end and 2 Nov coupon settlement test the 3.92% SOFR print.
Fiscal outlook and term premium; mostly a red/green contract story.
September added only 29,000; another soft report would revive the 2027 rally.
Brent at $115.81 is the main risk to fading 2027 hikes; $120 is the pain point.
